cases.question: Why does the Moon always show the same face to Earth?

sources.title: Tidal locking explained
sources.text: The Moon is tidally locked to Earth. Its rotation period equals its orbital period of about 27.3 days, so the same hemisphere always faces Earth. Tidal forces from Earth slowed the Moon's early rotation until the two periods matched.

sources.title: Libration of the Moon
sources.text: Because of libration, observers on Earth can see about 59 percent of the lunar surface over time. Libration comes from the Moon's elliptical orbit and the tilt of its axis.

sources.title: Moon myths
sources.text: Some people say the Moon does not rotate at all. That is a common myth about the night sky.

gold_claims.text: Earth's tides slowed the Moon's rotation

Tidal forces from Earth slowed the Moon's early rotation until the two periods matched [1]. Over time libration lets observers see about 59 percent of the lunar surface [2].

cases.question: What do mitochondria do in a cell, and where does their DNA come from?

sources.title: Mitochondria
sources.text: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which cells use as a source of chemical energy. This happens through oxidative phosphorylation on the inner membrane.

sources.title: Mitochondrial DNA
sources.text: Mitochondria have their own small circular genome, called mitochondrial DNA. In humans it is inherited almost entirely from the mother. The endosymbiotic theory holds that mitochondria descend from free-living bacteria.

cases.question: How does Rust free memory without a garbage collector?

sources.title: Understanding ownership
sources.text: Each value in Rust has an owner. There can only be one owner at a time. When the owner goes out of scope, the value will be dropped and its memory is freed. This lets Rust make memory safety guarantees without needing a garbage collector.

sources.title: References and borrowing
sources.text: A reference lets you use a value without taking ownership of it. At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references.

gold_claims.text: Values are dropped when the owner goes out of scope

cases.question: What are the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis?

sources.title: Photosynthesis
sources.text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy. Plants take in carbon dioxide and water and, using sunlight, produce glucose and release oxygen. The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast.

sources.title: The Calvin cycle
sources.text: The Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugars in the stroma of the chloroplast. It does not need light directly, but it uses ATP and NADPH made by the light-dependent reactions.

gold_claims.text: Inputs are carbon dioxide and water

cases.question: What is BM25 and what does its k1 parameter control?

sources.title: Okapi BM25
sources.text: BM25 is a ranking function used by search engines to estimate the relevance of documents to a query. It ranks documents by the query terms in each document, adjusted by term frequency saturation and document length normalisation. The parameter k1 controls term frequency saturation, and b controls how much document length matters.

sources.title: TF-IDF
sources.text: TF-IDF weighs a term by how often it appears in a document and how rare it is across the collection.

gold_claims.text: BM25 ranks documents by relevance to a query

cases.question: How does the SM-2 algorithm schedule a flashcard after a good answer?

sources.title: The SM-2 algorithm
sources.text: In SM-2 each card has an ease factor that starts at 2.5. After the first successful review the next interval is 1 day, after the second it is 6 days, and after that each new interval is the previous interval multiplied by the ease factor. A failed review resets the repetition count.
